chapter: Return to Atlanta and move north
title: Slim and Shorty come back and Lucille Achet says it is time for New York
summary: J. D. and Harvey return angry at Ella B. Moore, and Achet says it is time to go to New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So this was a period of time when you had already experienced the entertainment form, and now you went back to home, and you were just -- basically you became a kid again. You were going back to school then?
Well, when was the next time that you started tap dancing again really? I mean you danced on the street, you say, for coins then, but then what was the next break you had as introduction?
Well, it was Miss Lucille Achet, this lady had the record shop. She was telling me about her father was going to go to New York, see. And it was time for that.
Well, they -- they eventually came back. See, that's the thing about it.

Yeah, Slim and Shorty, they eventually came back, you see, and they were very angry, you know, at Chinch and Ella B, well, not actually at Chinch, you know. They was angry at Ella B. Moore because she continued to do this, you know, so they say they stopped going out dancing around, say, 'We didn't do it anymore after you left, you know.
So we figure we're going to leave too, you see. Anyhow, I got back with Miss Lucille Achet, and she said that it was time like to go to New York City, see.
